patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: (Mom) He has had a cold and fever, then his arms and legs shook for about a minute and his eyes rolled back. It stopped on its own. He is still sleepy but wakes when I talk to him. It was terrifying.
presentation.triageNote: 2-year-old boy with a temperature of 39.5 C after approximately one minute of generalized shaking and eye-rolling that stopped without treatment. He remains sleepy but rousable, with no rash or neck stiffness.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because the child remains postictal with altered responsiveness after a seizure and has a high fever, requiring rapid reassessment rather than routine resource-based sorting.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This febrile toddler had a brief generalized seizure and remains sleepy but rousable, requiring prompt reassessment of neurologic recovery and the fever source.
clinical.acuityReason: The seizure has stopped and breathing is adequate, but the child has not yet returned to baseline responsiveness and has a temperature of 39.5 C.
expectedResources: Focused evaluation for the source of fever
Laboratory or other testing if examination suggests serious infection
keyFindings: Approximately one minute of generalized shaking
No rash or neck stiffness reported
redFlags: High fever in a young child
teachingPoints: A brief generalized febrile seizure may ultimately be benign, but triage must reflect the child's current mental status rather than the eventual diagnosis.
Failure to return to baseline, focal seizure activity, recurrence, meningismus, petechiae, or respiratory compromise would heighten concern.

possibleDiagnoses: Simple febrile seizure with ongoing postictal recovery
Serious infection if additional findings emerge
possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: The child would be observed until back to baseline while the fever source is assessed; discharge may be appropriate after reassuring recovery and examination, with caregiver education and return precautions.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: 2-year-old boy, flushed with fever, in pajamas
aiImageGeneration.pose: drowsy on the clinic chair, leaning back
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a black 2-year-old boy in pajamas, flushed with fever, seated leaning back on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: drowsy, leaning back, limp and sleepy. Expression: dazed and sleepy, a postictal look. Clearly visible: flushed cheeks and heavy, drowsy eyes. No text, no logos.
